questions.q: What is one primary function of a constitution regarding government power?
questions.a: A constitution limits the power of the government so it cannot pass arbitrary or unfair laws against its citizens. A wrong answer often reveals the misconception that a government has absolute, unlimited power simply because it won an election.

questions.q: Why is coordination and trust among diverse groups considered a major function of a written constitution?
questions.a: A constitution provides a basic set of rules that all ethnic, linguistic, and religious groups agree to follow, preventing minority groups from feeling dominated by the majority. A wrong answer shows the misunderstanding that a country can stay unified simply through police force without a shared legal framework.

questions.q: If the Parliament of India passes a law that bans people from practicing a specific religion, which key function of the constitution prevents this law from staying valid?
questions.a: The constitution sets limits on government power and protects fundamental rights, rendering any law that violates these basic principles unconstitutional and void through judicial review. A wrong answer reveals the misconception that whatever Parliament passes automatically becomes absolute truth without constitutional bounds.

questions.q: How does a constitution establish who has the authority to make laws in a democratic country?
questions.a: It clearly defines the decision-making power, specifying whether citizens, monarchs, or elected representatives in a legislature hold the authority to legislate. A wrong answer indicates confusion between executive administrative duties and legislative law-making powers.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "A country does not need a written constitution if its leaders are honest and well-intentioned." Why is this argument flawed from a civic perspective?
questions.a: This argument is flawed because power can corrupt even well-intentioned leaders, and future leaders may not share the same values; a constitution provides permanent structural limits and institutional checks regardless of who is in power. A wrong answer shows a belief in benevolent dictatorship rather than constitutional democracy.

questions.q: Design a short rule for a hypothetical new nation that fulfills the constitutional function of "enabling the government to fulfill society's aspirations for social justice."
questions.a: A good answer proposes a foundational mandate requiring the state to provide free primary education or healthcare to all children regardless of wealth. A poor answer focuses only on punishment of crime rather than enabling social welfare and justice.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A ______ serves essential functions for a nation by laying down core rules that ensure coordination among citizens, specifying who has the power to make laws, placing limits on governmental authority, and enabling the government to fulfill the aspirations of a society for a just and inclusive future.

Fill in the blank: Imagine playing a cricket match in your neighborhood where there are no agreed-upon rules, no ______ lines, and no umpire; chaos would quickly erupt because everyone would play by their own wishes.
Fill in the blank: Building on what you learned in Grade ______ about why we need a government, we now explore how the constitution places boundaries on that very government.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Students can explain how a constitution limits government power and coordinates social behavior, using concrete examples from the Indian political system to demonstrate why nations cannot function without fundamental rules.
